clue.text: Novel for the first of April?

definitions.text: Novel for the first of April?

parts.words: Novel for the first of April?
parts.note: the first of April is a single date in the spring season, and the clue asks for the title of a novel naming such a date

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a novel, and April the first falls on one date of the season after winter.

clue.text: A fog and bit of drizzle shrouding a vessel

indicators.note: shrouding means the first group of letters wraps around the second a

parts.note: fog means mist

indicators.note: a bit of the word drizzle is its first letter

explanation.surface: A foggy, drizzly day blankets a boat at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives D, the first letter of drizzle; 'shrouding' puts the second A between MIST and D. The Amistad was the ship of the 1839 slave revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amistad was a Spanish schooner, a ship famous for the 1839 revolt by the captives aboard.

clue.text: Ball confiscated by one posh Italian linesman

indicators.note: a thing confiscated by someone is taken into their keeping, so the ball goes inside the posh person

parts.note: one posh person is an aristo, short for aristocrat
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A snooty Italian line judge seizes the ball during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' is not a sports official but a writer of lines of verse: Ludovico Ariosto wrote Orlando Furioso.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariosto was a Renaissance Italian poet, and a writer of verse lines can be jokingly called a linesman.

clue.text: Part of a castle guarded by private Harry Bailly?

indicators.note: something guarded by another thing sits inside it, so the castle part goes within the word for private

parts.note: private thoughts are inner ones
the keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A soldier called Harry stands guard over part of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private Harry' reads as a soldier; Harry Bailly is the host of the Tabard Inn in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Bailly keeps the Tabard Inn in Chaucer, an example of a landlord running a tavern.

clue.text: One like Marcus Aurelius upset one in Beds

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the overturned beds
upset in a down clue means the word for beds is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: cots are small beds
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor-philosopher is knocked over while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns COTS to STOC, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Aurelius wrote the Meditations and is a leading philosopher of the Stoa school.

clue.text: Soldiers live with cold around Winter

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers
to live is to be
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: Troops survive the freezing season as best they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winter' looks like the season, but it is a surname: Rebecca de Winter is the dead first wife in Daphne du Maurier's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of du Maurier's novel is the late Mrs de Winter, first wife of Maxim.

clue.text: Men with family south of southern tip of Melton Mowbray?

indicators.note: south of in a down clue means placed below, so the men and family come after
in a down clue the southern tip is the bottom, here the final letter of Melton

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, enlisted men in the army
folk can mean one's family

explanation.surface: Men and their families live south of the Leicestershire town famous for pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: Melton Mowbray looks like one place name, but Mowbray is split off as the definition: Thomas Mowbray was Duke of Norfolk in Shakespeare's Richard II. Melton Mowbray is a Leicestershire market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mowbray held the dukedom named after that East Anglian county and appears under that title in Richard II.

clue.text: A nice host who distributed work of Professor Laurana

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread around and laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A generous host hands out the portions so everyone gets their own share.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Laurana is the hero of Leonardo Sciascia's mafia novel A ciascuno il suo, known in English by this title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the English title of Sciascia's novel whose protagonist is the schoolteacher Laurana.

clue.text: Work popular with one at work is Persuasion

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
in means fashionable or popular
one is the Roman numeral I
a machine at work is on

explanation.surface: A popular work of fiction at work is Jane Austen's Persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persuasion' looks like Austen's novel, but here it means a belief someone holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion can be a firmly held belief or view.

clue.text: Angry young man Australiatransported in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the words should be said out loud and their sound taken

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia, and borne means transported or carried

explanation.surface: An angry youth was shipped off to Australia, as if heard in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs 'Australia' and 'transported' together as printed. John Osborne, author of Look Back in Anger, was the best known of the 1950s Angry Young Men.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright John Osborne was the leading figure of the 1950s writers dubbed the Angry Young Men.

clue.text: Grin with noveldue out, it's about unrequited obsession

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered, put out of their usual arrangement

explanation.surface: A smile goes with a book that is overdue, a story of hopeless longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noveldue' is printed as one word. Ian McEwan's novel concerns Jed Parry's fixation on Joe Rose, a case of de Clerambault's syndrome.
explanation.definitionFit: McEwan's novel centres on a stranger's fixated, one-sided love for the narrator Joe.

clue.text: Some blackheart is terrorising Archie Rice?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A villain is frightening a man named Archie Rice.
explanation.walkthrough: Archie Rice is the seedy music-hall comedian in John Osborne's play The Entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie Rice is a stage entertainer, a performer of music-hall turns.

clue.text: "It is the green-eyed monster which doth mock / The meat it feeds on; that — lives in bliss" (Othello)

definitions.text: "It is the green-eyed monster which doth mock / The meat it feeds on; that — lives in bliss" (Othello)

parts.words: "It is the green-eyed monster which doth mock / The meat it feeds on; that — lives in bliss" (Othello)
parts.note: Iago's lines on jealousy: the missing word is the deceived husband who is happy because he does not know of his wife's infidelity

explanation.definitionFit: Iago says the betrayed husband who is certain of his fate and does not love his wronger lives content.

clue.text: Laugh about year with doctor in health resort

indicators.note: about means the laugh goes around the year and the doctor

parts.note: ho is a laugh, as in ho ho

explanation.surface: A doctor laughs with a patient about the year spent at a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a hotel or spa offering water treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a hydropathic establishment, a spa hotel offering water cures.

clue.text: One going into space catches a disease and she documents regeneration

indicators.note: catches means the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a driver going into a parking space is a parker
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: An astronaut picks up an illness, and a woman records cell regrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into space' suggests an astronaut, but it is someone parking a car. Pat Barker wrote the Regeneration trilogy about the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Barker's Regeneration novels chronicle wartime shell-shock treatment at Craiglockhart hospital.

clue.text: "What both from Men and Angels I receive, / - of fire, air, flood, and on the earth" (Milton)

definitions.text: "What both from Men and Angels I receive, / - of fire, air, flood, and on the earth" (Milton)

parts.words: "What both from Men and Angels I receive, / - of fire, air, flood, and on the earth" (Milton)
parts.note: Satan in Paradise Lost lists the rulers of the elements who pay him homage; the gap is the word for those rulers

explanation.definitionFit: In Paradise Lost Satan names the rulers of the four elements, each a governor of a quarter.

clue.text: Read Lawrence in newly-issued reprint

indicators.note: in places the Lawrence letters inside the rearranged reprint
newly-issued signals that the word reprint is put out again in a new form

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials TE

explanation.surface: Read T. E. Lawrence in a freshly printed new edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' looks like a past or present verb about books, but it means to construe; T. E. Lawrence is Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation is to construe or understand its meaning.

clue.text: Queen article probing singer is awful at the start

indicators.note: probing means the article pushes its way into the other letters

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, a singer

indicators.note: at the start takes the first letter of is and of awful

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article investigating a singer finds she was dreadful from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania rules the fairies as their monarch in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Doctor and lawyer collecting very English poetry collection

indicators.note: collecting means the doctor and lawyer letters gather the others inside

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or tamper with
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A doctor and a lawyer gather some very English verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rig-Veda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rig-Veda is an ancient anthology of Sanskrit hymns, the earliest of the Vedas.

clue.text: Pile of crime novels primarily about distinctive character

indicators.note: about means the first letters go round the character word
primarily picks the first letter of crime and of novels

parts.note: an air is a distinctive quality or manner

explanation.surface: A stack of crime fiction is mainly about a distinctive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A cairn is a heap of stones built as a marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of stones raised as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Wild idea that man on Times put by conservative

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the Times word below the man word, so it comes after

parts.note: that man is him
times, as in an age or period, is an era

explanation.surface: A Tory places a far-fetched notion about a man in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put by' sets C beside the rest, at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful, impossible notion, like the fire-breathing monster of myth.

clue.text: Russian diplomat that detains old Cedric's son

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name

indicators.note: detains means the diplomat holds the old letter inside

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A Russian diplomat holds an old man's son prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's novel Wilfred of Ivanhoe is the disinherited son of Cedric the Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred of Ivanhoe is the son Cedric the Saxon disowns in Walter Scott's novel.

clue.text: Quantities of missing goods gone for a long time?

definitions.meaning: amounts of stock lost in transit or storage
read as two words, away for years on end

explanation.definitionFit: An outage is an amount lost in storage, and away for eons reads as two words.

clue.text: Woman with famous uncle put away by police finally

parts.note: to stow is to put away

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of police

explanation.surface: A woman known for her uncle is locked up by the police in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe is famous for her novel about Uncle Tom.

clue.text: Sue's daughter has trouble getting on a mammoth

indicators.note: getting on means the trouble is placed after, climbing on top of the rest

parts.note: mammoth means very big
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A girl is having trouble climbing onto a woolly mammoth.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mike Leigh's play Abigail's Party, Abigail is the unseen teenage daughter of the neighbour Sue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Leigh's play the neighbour Sue's teenage girl is holding the offstage party of the title.

clue.text: Doctor visited by working girl, one lacking nobility

indicators.note: visited by means the working girl letters go into the doctor's

parts.note: Dr No is the Bond villain, so the doctor here is No
a machine working is on
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A doctor is called on by a working girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' gives NO from Dr No, the James Bond villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person is an antihero, a protagonist without heroic qualities.

clue.text: Chap with famous uncle Bill spoilt, I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told means the words are heard spoken, so their sound matters

parts.note: check is an American word for a restaurant bill, and spoilt food has gone off

explanation.surface: A man with a well-known uncle says the bill went bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Anton Chekhov wrote the play Uncle Vanya.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov wrote Uncle Vanya, so his name is tied to that famous stage uncle.

clue.text: Awfully sad tales are written about A. Potter?

indicators.note: written about means the rearranged letters are set down around the A
awfully signals the words sad tales are are jumbled badly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sad tales have been written about a certain A. Potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges SAD TALES ARE to SARTEASDALE, and 'written about' puts A inside. The poet Sara Teasdale belonged to The Potters, a St Louis group of young women artists.
explanation.definitionFit: The American poet was a member of The Potters, who published the magazine The Potter's Wheel.
